research_question: Across a predeclared ordered load campaign, which changes remain visible across declared physical projections, where do those projections agree or disagree, and where does the numerical evidence stop?

cases.selection_note: Small manually inspectable development case. Previously used in Phase III; available for implementation checks and method development.

Prospective evaluation role for the new geometry method. Previously used by other Phase III methods, so it is not claimed to be historically untouched. No Phase V geometry parameter may be changed after its result is inspected.

projections.entity_alignment: one system row per converged load scale
projections.normalization: z-score using IEEE-9 development means and population standard deviations; zero-variance feature is an explicit insufficiency
projections.fit_scope: fit on IEEE-9 only; freeze and apply unchanged to IEEE-14
projections.information_loss: removes bus and line identity and compresses each solved network to seven aggregate features

projections.entity_alignment: stable pandapower bus index within each case
projections.fit_scope: case-local profile; dimensions are not compared directly across cases
projections.information_loss: omits angles, injections, line flows, and topology beyond ordered bus identity

operators.insufficiency_policy: return insufficient when either point is failed, unaligned, or contains a zero-variance projection feature
return insufficient for missing points or non-positive axis spacing

operators.formula: L_k = sum(i=1..k) ||z_i - z_(i-1)||_2 over the contiguous converged segment
operators.insufficiency_policy: stop the segment at a failed or missing point; do not bridge gaps
return insufficient when either displacement norm is zero or any of three points is unavailable
return insufficient when direction change or local arc-length denominator is unavailable
return not-applicable until a failed point follows a converged point

supported_claims: The declared adapter and solver produce reproducible benchmark computations under the locked environment.
Predeclared projections expose different aspects of the same ordered IEEE load campaign.
The listed discrete geometry operators can describe local change or explicit insufficiency on the sampled campaign.
The frozen method can be applied to IEEE-14 without Phase V parameter retuning after evaluation begins.
prohibited_claims: The load axis is elapsed time or an observed operational trajectory.
Pandapower non-convergence is a certified physical voltage-stability boundary.
A geometric change is a causal precursor, failure probability, or control recommendation.
IEEE benchmark behavior establishes real-world grid generalization.
The tube metaphor is a physical tube, globally smooth manifold, or universal field.
The evaluation case is historically untouched.
A benchmark computation is an observed outcome eligible for episodic memory.
evaluation_rules: Develop operator code and thresholds using IEEE-9 only.
Freeze projection definitions, normalization statistics, operator formulas, thresholds, and failure policy before inspecting Phase V IEEE-14 geometry outputs.
Apply identical code and configuration to IEEE-14 without case-specific branches or retuning.
Report success, failure, and indeterminate or insufficient results as first-class outcomes.
Preserve every non-converged snapshot and never fabricate physical values.
Generate JSON, Markdown, and figures from the same canonical run.
A later revised method requires a new manifest version and a new evaluation protocol.
